summary: Full save→display parity sweep on TestSeries fixture (LP-3611 / LP-6611). Backend pytest 17/18 pass, one real bug found: sale-display fields do NOT compute discount_percentage/sale_savings in preview serializer, and the storefront PDP does NOT render the WAS-price strikethrough nor a %-OFF sale chip. Every other attribute — color, finish (incl. finishes[] multi-value), material, thickness, slip_rating (R10), suitability, made_in (Italy flag row rendered near price), tiles_per_box (auto-computed sqm_per_box=1.08 for 30x60), custom_specs (FROST PROOF card), field_label_overrides (finish → SURFACE), list_price↔price↔room_lot_price both directions, draft path with is_draft=true full pass-through — SAVES AND DISPLAYS correctly. Fixture fully restored (LP-3611 price=49.99, LP-6611 price=28.99, colors/custom_specs/field_label_overrides cleared).

minor.issue: When sale_active=true and was_price is set, serializer returns discount_percentage=None and sale_savings=None. Expected: discount_percentage = round((was_price-price)/was_price*100) = ~19% for was 52.99 / price 42.99. Verified via API: {price:42.99, was_price:52.99, sale_active:true, discount_percentage:null, sale_savings:null, was_markup_percent:null}. This appears to break the frontend sale chip render.

ui_bugs.issue: With sale_active=true & was_price=52.99 & list_price=42.99 saved on LP-3611, the PDP shows '£42.99/m²' but does NOT render the crossed-out WAS £52.99 nor a '% OFF' badge/chip. The Volume Pricing table renders correctly (Your Price £42.99, Extra 5/10/15% off tiers) but the requested sale visualisation is missing. Likely because backend returns discount_percentage=null (see backend minor issue) and the sale-strike component may be gated on that field being truthy.
ui_bugs.selector: PDP price area near '£42.99/m²' / expected .line-through span with £52.99

action_items: FIX serializer_tile_for_shop in /app/backend/tiles.py to compute discount_percentage and sale_savings when sale_active=true and was_price>price (formula: round((was-price)/was*100) for %, was-price for £ savings). Currently these come back as null in preview API output.

VERIFY the CollectionDetailPage sale-display component: even when discount_percentage is present, ensure the WAS £{was_price} strikethrough and % OFF chip actually render (they were absent in the current build with sale_active=true, was_price=52.99). Suspected root cause: component reads discount_percentage which was null.
critical_code_review_comments: backend serializer: sale_savings & discount_percentage & was_markup_percent should ALWAYS be derived server-side when sale_active is true, not left as raw persisted fields, to avoid frontend having to duplicate the math.

PDP defaulted to a 60x120 sibling product instead of LP-3611 even when ?sku=LP-3611 was passed in the URL — the sku URL param is not respected by the initial-product selector. Not a blocker (user can click the 30x60 size chip) but worth wiring.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Sale-display bug is the single outstanding issue from the parity sweep. Once main agent fixes serializer to emit discount_percentage/sale_savings for sale_active=true rows AND ensures PDP renders the strikethrough+%-OFF chip, re-run test_sale_fields_flow in /app/backend/tests/test_save_display_parity.py plus a quick browser check on /shop/collection/TestSeries?preview=1 → select 30x60 size → confirm WAS £52.99 strikethrough visible and a % OFF chip near the £42.99 price. Also note: PDP initial-product routing via ?sku= URL param is not honoured — user has to click the size chip to switch products.
rca of the issue: Sale strike/chip missing on PDP root cause: /api/tiles/collection/{series}?preview=1 serializer returns discount_percentage=null and sale_savings=null even when sale_active=true & was_price>price are persisted. Frontend sale-badge JSX in CollectionDetailPage.js appears to gate on discount_percentage being truthy → nothing renders. Fix in serialize_tile_for_shop (tiles.py ~line 97): after resolving price and was_price, if sale_active and was_price>0 and was_price>price: discount_percentage = round((was_price-price)/was_price*100, 0); sale_savings = round(was_price-price, 2).
